title: Serbian Despots
capsule: The Serbian Despotate was formally established in 1402 when Byzantine Emperor Manuel II granted the title Despot to Stefan Lazarević, who had submitted to Ottoman suzerainty after Kosovo (1389) and served Bayezid I at Ankara. Stefan received Belgrade from Hungary in 1403 and ruled from there, commissioning the Resava monastery and fostering a notable literary and scholarly culture. After Stefan's death in 1427, his nephew Đurađ Branković built the capital Smederevo Fortress (completed 1430) and maintained a precarious existence against Ottoman encroachment until the despotate was finally extinguished by the Ottoman conquest of Smederevo in 1459; the attested window of 1375–1422 covers the Lazarević period from after Kosovo to shortly before Stefan's death.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The despotate's core territory in Serbia proper is well documented through Byzantine, Ottoman, and Serbian sources; frontier zones fluctuated significantly with Ottoman campaigns and are reconstructed rather than precisely mapped.
